candidates.description: Cultivar-specific AAS winner evidence for Mountain Merit.
candidates.source_locator: AAS Winner Data > Mountain Merit F1

traits.source_excerpt: AAS reports 75 days from transplant to harvest.
AAS reports fruit 3 to 3.5 inches in diameter.
AAS reports fruit weighing 10 to 12 ounces.
AAS reports harvest over a four- to five-week period.
AAS reports plants four to five feet tall.
AAS recommends two feet between plants.
AAS reports plants two to three feet wide.
Mountain Merit was the 2014 AAS Heartland regional winner.
AAS lists resistance and moderate resistance to six disease or nematode concerns.
AAS recommends the fruit for slicing and sandwiches.

candidates.description: Observed Virginia home-garden trial evidence for Provider.
candidates.source_locator: PDF page 2 > Table 1 > Provider

traits.source_excerpt: Provider was evaluated in the 2025 Virginia community-engaged home-garden trial.
The trial observed an average of 59 days to harvest.
The trial table lists no known disease resistance for Provider.
Trial participants gave Provider a 5.97 overall rating.
Seventy-eight percent of trial participants recommended Provider.
The published observation covers the 2025 trial year.

candidates.description: Observed Virginia home-garden trial evidence for Marketmore 76.
candidates.source_locator: PDF page 2 > Table 1 > Marketmore 76

traits.source_excerpt: The trial table lists CMV, powdery mildew, and scab resistance.
Marketmore 76 was evaluated in the 2025 Virginia community-engaged home-garden trial.
The trial observed an average of 64 days to harvest.
The trial table lists CMV, powdery mildew, and scab resistance.
Trial participants gave Marketmore 76 a 6.13 overall rating.
Eighty-two percent of trial participants recommended Marketmore 76.
The published observation covers the 2025 trial year.
